claim: Thibault et al. trained a REEM-C humanoid Brax/MJX PPO policy for 200,000,000 steps with 8192 parallel environments, completing in approximately 56 minutes on an RTX 4090.
stance_target: 200M steps is sufficient for humanoid locomotion convergence in Brax/MJX PPO
scope_conditions: REEM-C humanoid, 12-DOF legs, MJX simulator, Brax PPO, single RTX 4090, AMD 7950x CPU, 64GB RAM
quoted_support: The training is run for 200,000,000 training steps with 8192 parallel environments using PPO. The networks for the PPO algorithm had 4 hidden layers of 128 neurons. This training was performed on a PC with an AMD 7950x CPU, 64 GB RAM, and an RTX 4090 24 GB VRAM and completed training in approximately 56 minutes.

claim: The Brax/MJX humanoid paper reports no BC pretrain or DR finetune stage; it is a single PPO run with domain randomization integrated into the environment.
stance_target: stage decomposition in Brax/MJX humanoid training
scope_conditions: Single-stage PPO training with optimized robot model (lower body only) and MJX performance tuning
quoted_support: Note that to achieve fast and high performance training an optimized model of the robot was used, containing only lower body collisions and recommended MJX performance tuning techniques

claim: The Brax/MJX humanoid paper is the most directly hardware-comparable to the user's hexapod project: same Brax PPO + MJX stack, similar GPU class (RTX 4090 vs RTX 5060 Ti), similar num_envs=8192.
stance_target: 200M step budget at 8192 envs is a reasonable reference point for the user's hexapod project
scope_conditions: Brax PPO, MJX, single consumer GPU
quoted_support: The RL algorithms of Brax using the MJX simulator, a version of MuJoCo that supports the XLA compiler for GPU and TPU based simulation using JAX, is used to train the locomotion policy.
